newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Three brokerage directors fined by S.Africa's JSE.
newsitem.headline: Three brokerage directors fined by S.Africa's JSE.

text.p: Three Frankel Pollack directors and the stock brokerage itself have been fined after pleading guilty to breaking the rules and conventions of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the bourse said on Thursday.
The offences by Sidney Frankel, Geoff Rothschild and George Frantzeskou occurred during 1989 to 1991 and relate mainly to acitvites by former directors G.L. Blank and F.J.T. Kruger.
The JSE said it had taken into account Sidney Frankel's tip off that he had become suspicious about the work of Blank.
"Neither the charges nor the admissions related to complicity by any of the firm's directors in Blank actvities," the exchange said.

As a firm Frankel Pollack, in which France's Societie Generale recently bought a 51 percent stake, has admitted failing to establish control over or monitor Kruger's trading and failing to spot Blank's untoward operation of Capital Nominees, a client account.
Frankel Pollack has agreed to pay out 250,000 rand to the JSE's Guarantee Fund.
After pleading guilty to related charges Sidney Frankel and Rothschild are both to pay a 40,000 rand fine to the fund and Frantzeskou is to pay 10,000 rand.
